title: Topical rectal stump therapy after subtotal colectomy and pouch outcomes in ulcerative colitis: a prospective observational cohort study
summary: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammation of the large bowel. When medication no longer works well enough, the large bowel is removed surgically. In severely ill patients this is usually done in three steps: first, the large bowel is removed except for the rectum and a stoma (an artificial bowel opening) is created. A few weeks later, a reservoir („pouch") is formed from the last part of the small bowel and joined to the anus, the rectum is removed at this stage. After several more months the stoma is closed. Between the first and second step the rectum remains in the body but is still inflamed. At our hospital this inflammation is treated according to a fixed standard of care with suppositories and foam that act directly in the rectum. A common late problem after pouch surgery is inflammation of the reservoir („pouchitis"). We want to find out whether patients whose rectum was treated in this way before pouch surgery develop such an inflammation less often in the first year after stoma closure than would be expected from previous experience. To do so, we observe 88 adult patients treated according to this standard at Heidelberg University Hospital. The study does not change treatment: all examinations, medicines and operations are part of normal care. We only additionally analyse the treatment data and tissue samples that arise anyway.

interventions.name: Patients with ulcerative colitis in a three-stage surgical pathway (status after subtotal colectomy, planned restorative proctocolectomy with IPAA). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Histologically confirmed diagnosis of ulcerative colitis
Refractory disease course (failure of ≥ 1 biologic or small molecule, or acute fulminant colitis with indication for surgery)
Planned restorative proctocolectomy (IPAA) as a three-stage procedure (status after subtotal colectomy)
Existing signed consent for the tissue and blood biobank of the Department of Surgery (broad consent in the version valid at the time of inclusion)
Sufficient ability to understand the nature and individual consequences of the study
Exclusion criteria:
Known hypersensitivity or allergy to mesalazine, budesonide or their excipients
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Confirmed or clinically probable diagnosis of Crohn's disease or indeterminate colitis
Severe comorbidities (ASA ≥ IV) precluding study participation on medical grounds
Lack of capacity to consent
